procedure_column: Navarro et al. 2024 (ACS ESC 8) Iron meteorites Raster mapping (2D) ns-LA-SF-ICP-MS University of Campinas

Procedure Name.cell: Navarro et al. (2024) Iron Meteorite Raster Mapping v1
Procedure Name.value: Navarro et al. (2024) Iron Meteorite Raster Mapping v1

Laboratory.cell: Isotope Geology Laboratory, University of Campinas (UNICAMP), Brazil
Laboratory.value: Isotope Geology Laboratory, University of Campinas (UNICAMP), Brazil

Procedure Reference(s).cell: Navarro et al. (2024) ACS Earth Space Chem. 8, 281; Longerich et al. (1996)
Procedure Reference(s).value: Navarro et al. (2024) ACS Earth Space Chem. 8, 281; Longerich et al. (1996)

Sampling Unit Type.cell: Region of interest > Phase — "elemental mapping, conducted within regions featuring diverse phases of the Augusto Pestana meteorite" (p.1); the map is read for the phases it resolves, "even without prior knowledge regarding natural structural variations" (p.1)

Sample Preparation Method.cell: Same Augusto Pestana fragment etched with Nital solution (2% v/v HNO₃ in ethanol) to reveal kamacite and plessite
Sample Preparation Method.value: Same Augusto Pestana fragment etched with Nital solution (2% v/v HNO₃ in ethanol) to reveal kamacite and plessite

Sampling Unit Selection Criteria.cell: Representativeness, and phase diversity — "the approach of rastering large areas may improve representative sampling compared with spot analysis" (p.2), and the mapping is "conducted within regions featuring diverse phases of the Augusto Pestana meteorite" (p.1)

Pre-Analysis Imaging and Screening.cell: Chemical etching to reveal the phases before mapping — "For the mapping experiment, the polished surface of the Augusto Pestana sample was etched with freshly prepared Nital solution (2% v/v HNO3 ... in 99.5% absolute ethanol) to reveal the presence of different phases (in this case, kamacite and plessite)" (p.3). Not imaging, but the screening step that sites the map
Pre-Analysis Imaging and Screening.value: Chemical etching to reveal the phases before mapping

Interface Cone Configuration.cell: Ni sampler cone; Ni skimmer cone
Interface Cone Configuration.value: Ni sampler cone; Ni skimmer cone

Detector Configuration.cell: Triple mode detector (pulse counting, analog, Faraday)
Detector Configuration.value: Triple mode detector (pulse counting, analog, Faraday)

Laser Wavelength and Type.cell: 193 nm ArF excimer; pulse duration 4 ns
Laser Wavelength and Type.value: 193 nm ArF excimer; pulse duration 4 ns

Raster Line Spacing (Mapping Only).cell: N (line spacing not stated; 150 µm spot at 10 µm s⁻¹)

Carrier Gas and Flow Rate.cell: He: 0.6 l min⁻¹ (MFC 1) + 0.7 l min⁻¹ (MFC 2) in HelEx II cell
Carrier Gas and Flow Rate.value: He: 0.6 l min⁻¹ (MFC 1) + 0.7 l min⁻¹ (MFC 2) in HelEx II cell

Make-up Gas and Flow Rate.cell: Ar make-up gas (same as spot protocol)
Make-up Gas and Flow Rate.value: Ar make-up gas (same as spot protocol)

Coolant (Plasma) Gas Flow Rate.cell: Plasma gas: 16 l min⁻¹; Auxiliary: 0.9 l min⁻¹
Coolant (Plasma) Gas Flow Rate.value: Plasma gas: 16 l min⁻¹; Auxiliary: 0.9 l min⁻¹

Analysis Sequence.cell: Background (1 min) → NIST SRM 612(×3) → North Chile(×3) → unknown map (30 min) → North Chile(×3) → NIST SRM 612(×3) → background
Analysis Sequence.value: Background (1 min) → NIST SRM 612(×3) → North Chile(×3) → unknown map (30 min) → North Chile(×3) → NIST SRM 612(×3) → background

Target Species.cell: ⁵²Cr, ⁵⁷Fe, ⁵⁹Co, ⁶¹Ni, ⁶⁵Cu, ⁶⁹Ga, ⁷²Ge, ⁷⁵As, ⁹⁹Ru, ¹⁰³Rh, ¹⁰⁵Pd, ¹⁸²W, ¹⁸⁵Re, ¹⁸⁹Os, ¹⁹³Ir, ¹⁹⁵Pt, ¹⁹⁷Au (same 17 isotopes as spot protocol)

Monitored Masses.key: defines: monitored property per target species

Reported Variables and Units.cell: Elemental mass fractions per phase, obtained by integrating 176 kamacite points over 211,060 µm2 and 1,173 plessite points over 1,712,297 µm2 — As, Au, Co, Cu, Ga, Ge, Ir, Pd, Ru in µg g-1 and Fe, Ni in g/100 g, each with 2 sdm and the integrated area and point count (Table 5, p.12); phase identification from the maps (nominal)

value.member: obtained by integrating 176 kamacite points over 211

Dwell Time per Mass.cell: 0.02 s per isotope; 100 samples per peak (same as spot protocol)

Background Count Time.cell: 60 s background measurement before mapping session start; 3 measurements each for NIST and North Chile after background
Background Count Time.value: 60 s background measurement before mapping session start; 3 measurements each for NIST and North Chile after background

Internal Standard Approach.cell: Fe+Ni+Co sum normalization to 100% (same DRS as spot protocol; mandatory for multi-phase mapping without prior IS knowledge)

Internal Standard Element.cell: No single IS; Fe+Ni+Co=100% normalization (same as spot protocol)

Elemental Fractionation Correction.cell: Same calibration approach as spot protocol (iolite 3D DRS; same yield correction)

Signal Integration Interval Method.cell: Same procedure as spot protocol; signal integration for mapping not separately described
Signal Integration Interval Method.value: Same procedure as spot protocol; signal integration for mapping not separately described

Spike / Outlier Filtering Approach.cell: N (mapping; iolite 3D DRS handles background; no per-pixel spike filtering described)

Blank / Background Correction Method.cell: Background (1 min) measured at session start; additional 3 measurements of NIST and North Chile used for calibration (background included in regression line for gas blank)
Blank / Background Correction Method.value: Background (1 min) measured at session start; additional 3 measurements of NIST and North Chile used for calibration (background included in regression line for gas blank)

Interference Correction Method.cell: Same isotope selection as spot protocol

Memory Effect Mitigation.cell: N (mapping; ARIS-equivalent not described; single mapping session)

Normalization / Standards-Based Correcti.cell: Fe+Ni+Co=100% normalization (mandatory for multi-phase mapping); same iolite DRS as spot

Analysis Inclusion and Rejection Criteri.cell: Partially — the reported values integrate a stated number of points per phase, "176 kamacite points (211,060 µm2) and 1,173 plessite points (1,712,297 µm2)" (Table 5, p.12). The points are assigned to a phase rather than admitted or rejected, and no rejection rule is stated

Combination Method.cell: all: integrated over the map points assigned to each phase — Table 5: '176 kamacite points (211,060 µm2) and 1,173 plessite points (1,712,297 µm2)'

value.value: integrated over the map points assigned to each phase

Primary Calibration Standard Name.cell: NIST SRM 612 (Jochum et al. 2011) + North Chile Filomena — same as spot protocol

Calibration Standard Measurement Frequen.cell: NIST SRM 612 and North Chile at start and end of mapping session (30 min map; 3 measurements each before and after)
Calibration Standard Measurement Frequen.value: NIST SRM 612 and North Chile at start and end of mapping session (30 min map; 3 measurements each before and after)

Secondary Reference Materials.cell: North Chile and NIST SRM 612 measured before and after mapping session as QC materials

value.member: North Chile and NIST SRM 612 measured before and after mapping session as QC materials

Detection Limit.cell: N (LODs not separately reported for mapping)

Detection Limit Method.cell: N (LODs not separately reported for mapping)

Internal (Within-Measurement) Analytical.key: sample > sampling unit x reported property

Within-Session Analytical Precision and.cell: N (within-session precision for mapping not separately assessed)

Analytical Accuracy and Assessment Metho.cell: N (mapping accuracy not separately assessed from spot protocol)

Additional Notes.cell: Elemental mapping used as classification tool even without prior knowledge of structural variations (kamacite vs. plessite); demonstrates LA-ICP-MS mapping applicability for iron meteorite classification
Additional Notes.value: Elemental mapping used as classification tool even without prior knowledge of structural variations (kamacite vs. plessite); demonstrates LA-ICP-MS mapping applicability for iron meteorite classification
